claims.content: Complete transactions for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Complete transactions for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer selects the won auction item(s) they want to pay for, chooses a shipping method, chooses a payment type, and completes the checkout/payment transaction.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer is at checkout with at least one won auction item available to pay for.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has successfully completed checkout and payment for the selected won auction item(s).
in_scope_actions: choose which won auction items to pay for
variant_dimensions: selection of won item(s) paid in one checkout instance

claims.content: Customer
The Customer has at least one won auction item available to pay for.

The Customer has received a valid 2nd-Chance offer email (sent to a second-place finisher after the original winner failed to pay) enabling them to purchase the item at their last bid price, and the 72-hour response window has not yet expired.
The Customer accesses the payment page by clicking the 'Winnings Alert' link or via the 'pay now' link in the winner notification email.
The Customer selects the won auction item(s) they want to pay for by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item in the list of won items.
The system offers the Customer a choice of shipping methods.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option (e.g., USPS Standard or Expedited) via radio buttons.
The system gets the Customer started on the payment process for their winnings.

The Customer selects a checkout option by clicking either 'Check out with PayPal' or 'Check out with Amazon', completes the payment transaction with the selected payment provider, and after payment is successfully processed is returned to a Thank You page.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of selecting the won item(s) via the 'Pay Now' checkboxes on the payments page, the Customer completes checkout/payment for a 2nd-Chance offer item by clicking 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' in the automated email; the system automatically generates an order for the item without requiring the normal checkout steps.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of selecting the won item(s) via the 'Pay Now' checkboxes on the payments page, the Customer clicks 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' in the 2nd-Chance offer email; the system generates the order, loads the Sign-In page, and after the Customer signs in, takes the Customer to the Returning Winners Payments Page to pay for the order.

Diverges from Step 5: Instead of manually choosing a checkout option, a returning Customer whose default Method of Payment (MOP) is PayPal or Amazon Payments is automatically routed to a specific page that offers a choice of shipping methods and initiates the payment process for the Customer's winnings.
The Customer may select PayPal as their payment method by choosing the corresponding radio button in the 'My Payment Methods' section.

Diverges from Step 5: After choosing PayPal, the Customer who already has a PayPal account may log in using the email and password fields on the right side of the page, which is an alternative path to completing payment without creating a new account or using Amazon.

Diverges from Step 5: After choosing PayPal, the Customer may create a new PayPal account by selecting 'Create a PayPal account', entering the Country (defaulted to United States), and choosing a payment method ('Bill Me Later' or 'Credit Card') to complete payment.
Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may choose to pay using Amazon Payments, which opens a new browser session to register or log in to Amazon.

missing_aspects: Explicit evidence that the final payment-completion step is executed in the default-MOP and Amazon Payments alternative branches.
Evidence supporting that this selection leads to a successful transaction completion or constitutes a divergent flow from the main use case.

claims.content: At main_flow Step 5, if the Customer selects the 'Checkout Later' option instead of clicking 'Check out with PayPal' or 'Check out with Amazon', the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a message stating that payment can be made within 7 days (168 hours) but unpaid orders will be cancelled after that window.

After main_flow Step 5, if the Customer does not complete payment within 168 hours (including the default-MOP alternative, where the system has sent an email requiring sign-in and payment within 7 days and warning of negative consequences), the system cancels the order, places the item in Hold status, and if the Customer has expired PayPal/Amazon unpaid winnings over 7 days old, automatically locks the account into Review Status; the Customer cannot later pay for the cancelled order. Exit: use case terminates with a failed, non-completable transaction.

At main_flow Step 1, in the 2nd-Chance offer alternative, if the Customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after it is sent, the system returns the item to auction available inventory and reschedules it for a future auction. Exit: use case terminates; the 2nd-Chance checkout path is no longer available.

At main_flow Step 1, in the 2nd-Chance offer alternative, if the 2nd-place finisher's bid is below the item's unit cost, the system does not send the 2nd-Chance offer email, so the 2nd-Chance checkout/payment path cannot be initiated. Exit: use case does not enter the alternative flow.

missing_aspects: Explicit evidence for the use case termination/exit state upon selecting 'Checkout Later'.

claims.content: The 'Payment Status' column in the 'Items I've Won' table displays 'Paid' for items where the transaction has been successfully completed.
After the Customer completes the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the system displays a Thank You page with the global header/footer and a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
Upon the Customer accepting a 2nd-Chance offer by clicking 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card', the system automatically generates an order for the item and ships it.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The Main Flow ends at step 5 with the Customer selecting a checkout option ('Check out with PayPal' or 'Check out with Amazon'). It does not include completing the external payment flow or returning to the JTV site for the Thank You page. As a result, the Postconditions that require a 'Paid' status and a Thank You page cannot be reached from the Main Flow. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Evidence supporting that the system updates the Payment Status to 'Paid' upon completion.))

[goal_mainflow_alignment] The goal and its canonical success scenario require that the Customer completes the checkout/payment transaction, but main_flow ends at Step 5 with selecting a checkout option. No main-flow claim explicitly shows the transaction being completed after that selection. The main_flow coverage_state itself notes that evidence does not explicitly state that clicking the checkout buttons completes the transaction within this specific step. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Evidence supporting that the system updates the Payment Status to 'Paid' upon completion.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 1 describes the Customer selecting 'Checkout Later' and the system graying out the page, disabling links, and displaying a 168-hour message, but it does not explicitly state whether the use case terminates, suspends, returns to a main-flow step, or hands off. Without an explicit exit/terminal state, the branch lacks a clear outcome as required by the rule. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit confirmation that selecting 'Return to Payments' suspends the use case or resumes the session.; Explicit confirmation that selecting 'JTVauctions Homepage' terminates the use case.))

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Postcondition 3 describes a 2nd-Chance offer acceptance/payment path ('I accept, pay with my On File credit card') that does not appear anywhere in the Trigger or Main Flow. The Trigger only covers accessing the payment page via Winnings Alert or a winner-notification 'pay now' link, and Main Flow steps 1-5 only cover selecting won items, shipping, and PayPal/Amazon checkout. Therefore the Main Flow cannot lead to the automatic 2nd-Chance order/shipping postcondition.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 1 (Checkout Later) describes the system graying out the page, disabling links, and showing a 7-day payment message, but does not explicitly state the resulting control flow: whether the use case terminates, suspends until a later payment attempt, or returns to a main flow step. The branch therefore lacks a clear exit/return outcome.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger includes a 2nd-Chance offer email path (clicking 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' in a 2nd-Chance offer email), but the Preconditions only cover standard won-item checkout: 'at least one won auction item available to pay for.' A customer entering via a 2nd-Chance offer may not have a won item yet, and the 2nd-Chance order Postcondition is not supported by the standard Main Flow. The 2nd-Chance path is therefore not covered from the start of the use case.

The Trigger adds a 2nd-Chance offer entry path ('Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' in the offer email), but the Main Flow is written only for the standard won-item checkout and the goal scope contract covers only won auction items. The 2nd-Chance path is not continued in Main Flow step 1 and also leads to an inconsistent Postcondition 3 ('On File credit card' acceptance/order/ship). This is a discontinuity introduced by the Trigger's extra alternative.

The Main Flow ends at step 5 with the Customer selecting a PayPal/Amazon checkout option. It never includes the Customer completing the external payment/checkout process, so Postcondition 1 (Payment Status = Paid) and Postcondition 2 (Thank You page) are not actually reachable from the Main Flow.

The goal explicitly requires completing the checkout/payment transaction, but main_flow stops at Step 5 with the Customer selecting a checkout option ('Check out with PayPal' or 'Check out with Amazon') and does not include any final step stating that payment is completed, confirmed, or the transaction is finalized. Therefore the main flow is incomplete relative to the goal's success criterion.
